adjudicated_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let X be a smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of finite type over C, so that Betti cohomology H^i(X;Q) carries a functorial mixed Hodge structure. Let f: Z -> X be a finite-type morphism from an algebraic stack of finite type over C. Let Y be the unique reduced closed substack of X whose underlying space is the Zariski closure of the constructible geometric image of f, and let U = X minus Y. For all integers i and m and every Tate twist (n), restriction r: H^i(X;Q)(n) -> H^i(U;Q)(n) is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures. Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for the weight filtration (Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Theoreme 2.3.5), equivalently W_m is an exact functor, so ker(W_m r) equals the image of W_m H^i_Y(X;Q)(n) in W_m H^i(X;Q)(n) as a sub-mixed-Hodge structure. When H^i of the smooth stack X has weights at least i and m equals that lowest weight, W_m coincides with Gr^W_m. This identification uses only the closed-open localization triangle of the pair (Y,U) and requires no Gysin map, no regular-immersion or lci hypothesis on Y, no purity of codimension, and no closed immersion of Z. Every class in W_m H^i(X;Q)(n) supported on a closed substack of X contained in Y lies in the kernel. The kernel may strictly contain the span of classes supported on the image of Z; equality with that span, and exhaustion of W_m H^i(X;Q)(n) by the kernel, are separate assertions not supplied by this pattern. At (g,n)=(6,6), with X = M_{6,6}, i = 26, m = 26, twist (21), and f the classifying morphism of the ordered reduced-support Casnati-Ekedahl model, the pattern is the corroborated FND-0180 construction of T_Z, identified there with the FND-0168(3a) image of W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) in T.
contradiction_resolution: Inspected the originating artifacts before the packet backlog: ATT-0120 Sections 4-6 and CLM-0120-3/4/5 construct T_Z as ker(W_26 of ordinary restriction along M_{6,6} minus the reduced Zariski closure Y of the Casnati-Ekedahl classifying image) and identify it with the image of W_26 H^{26}_Y(M_{6,6};Q)(21); REV-0170 confirms those claims and extracts the candidate support-kernel-closure-pattern, explicitly warning that overlap with FND-0168(3a) could not be assessed in that pass. The contested identification is Deligne's strictness theorem (Theorie de Hodge II, Theoreme 2.3.5: morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, so W_m is exact on the abelian category of mixed Hodge structures), applied to the closed-open localization triangle, and is the standard meaning of support in Payne, arXiv:2605.20453v1, Section 2.1 (a rational sub-Hodge structure is supported on a closed algebraic subset Z when it lies in ker(H^j(X)->H^j(X minus Z))). Chevalley constructibility of a quasi-compact locally finitely presented image is Stacks Project Tag 054K; the unique reduced closed substack on the Zariski closure is then well-defined. The candidate's appeal to exactness of Gr^W_m is only the associated-graded form of strictness and coincides with the W_m statement on the lowest-weight piece of a smooth stack (weights of H^i at least i), but the original text never quantified the weight index m and so overstated the Gr^W justification. No contradiction with CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001: the pattern asserts no Tate type. It is compatible with THM-0001 (purity only for smooth proper stacks) and with FND-0165 (which withholds an independent compact-support mixed Hodge formalism for stacks, not ordinary cohomology of smooth finite-type stacks). Overlap with FND-0168(3a) is real but not identity: 0168(3a) is the Borel-Moore localization image at weight -16 on M_{6,6}. Packet-corroborated FND-0180 already records the ordinary-cohomology kernel T_Z for this classifying image, identifies it with the FND-0168(3a) image via Poincare-Verdier on the smooth pair, and states one-sided coverage, possible extra components of Y, and the absence of Gysin, lci, and a closed embedding of Z. Packet FND-0182 further records that the reduced classifying-image closure yields the unique smallest kernel-form term and that the kernel may strictly contain classes supported on the image of Z. The candidate is therefore the textbook engine of the already-corroborated FND-0180 instance, not a new obstruction, and is merged into FND-0180 rather than promoted as a general lemma: the originating attempt and review supply (g,n)=(6,6) evidence; FND-0165's stack-level compact-support caveat would have to be discharged for a fully general stack statement; and the inflation warning is already FND-0180/FND-0182.
